dedupe_keys.name: csb investigation west fertilizer company fire and explosion 2013

description: This case study is the U.S. Chemical Safety Board's investigation of the fire and explosion of fertiliser-grade ammonium nitrate at the West Fertilizer Company storage and distribution facility in West, Texas, on 17 April 2013, which killed 14 people, 12 of them volunteer firefighters, injured hundreds of people in the surrounding community. It was carried out by the U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board (CSB), which released its final report on 28 January 2016. The CSB page offers the final report as PDF, a safety video called Dangerously Close, and the public meeting presentation and transcript, all free. Caveats: the CSB does not assign blame or fines, and its findings rest on a site largely destroyed by the blast, so some causes remain undetermined. The investigation found gaps in regulation of ammonium nitrate storage, in separation distances between such facilities and homes and public buildings, and in firefighter training on the hazard, and it issued 19 recommendations on land-use planning, emergency response, OSHA and EPA rules, sprinklers, fire detection and non-combustible construction. For simulation it is a reference event for explosion hazard exposure, emergency response and land-use separation analyses around chemical facilities. It is related to the CSB Philadelphia Energy Solutions refinery record in this catalogue, another CSB post-event analysis.
